title: Who is actually responsible?
caption:
When a local policy changes or public infrastructure fails, outrage often targets the loudest official.

In local government, authority is legally divided. Mayors propose. City councils vote. School boards contract separately.

The Daily Nun traced how local jurisdictions work and where public dockets reside.

reel.title: Who signs the check?
reel.voiceover: When people get frustrated by a local decision, they usually tag the mayor. But in local government, authority is legally divided. Mayors propose budgets, but city councils vote on them. School boards award their own contracts. And transit runs on separate boards. The real question isn't who has the biggest microphone—it's who has the legal authority to sign the check. The Daily Nun.
kineticText: Before a dollar moves, it must appear on a public meeting agenda.
The minutes show who voted yes.
